groups.text: It is currently 23 degrees and cloudy in Berlin-Tempelhof.
With the morning weather set, here is the news.

Nvidia is pushing to tie open AI more tightly to its own hardware through a new open-source tool called PAIR. This Personal AI Router turns a home network into a mini data center by spreading local AI requests across all available devices, which prevents any single GPU from overloading. In one demo, a three-device cluster finished a task in under nine minutes, compared to eighteen minutes on a single laptop. The system supports Apple silicon starting with the M4 and GeForce RTX cards from the 20 series up. While Nvidia focuses on high-end hardware integration, Nigerian startup ChipMango is targeting the talent pipeline for the broader supply chain. ChipMango recently raised a 1.9 million dollar seed round to expand its AI-powered chip-design learning platform across Africa, Europe, and the United States. The company plans to grow its engineering teams and establish a design center in Malta.

The United Nations warns that the El Niño climate phenomenon in the Pacific is set to be historically intense this year. This shift threatens to disrupt winter weather across Europe and France, potentially bringing heavy rainfall and polar air incursions further south. In Britain, The Guardian reports a more dire outlook, describing it as the El Niño of the millennium. British ministers are now urging their citizens to stockpile food and water in anticipation of possible power outages during the winter months. These extreme climate events are being driven by global warming. Meanwhile, Friday's press headlines also focus on Italy's Giorgia Meloni and a leader currently facing difficulties.

Enterprises are struggling to manage security risks as cloud adoption accelerates. To address these gaps, a full-day virtual event on November 12 focuses on securing cloud assets in the age of AI and managing multi-cloud environments. This comes as agentic AI introduces new insider threat models for organizations, while nearly every organization faced a critical security incident last year with most lacking the equipment to contain them. Other recent disruptions include a Wi-Fi hack that affected Delta flights. In a separate matter involving the targeting of media professionals, an occupation court has sentenced Melitopol journalist Iryna Levchenko to 15 years in a penal colony. The court found her guilty of espionage on September 4. These events highlight a stark contrast between the technical vulnerabilities facing global corporate infrastructure and the direct legal perils faced by journalists reporting from occupied territories.

Technical updates for local AI are moving toward broader hardware compatibility. In the latest release of llama.cpp, developer Aaron Teo from IBM fixed an uninitialized v_acc issue for q5_1 on s390x CPUs. This specific patch addresses a bug in the ggml-cpu implementation to ensure stability on those systems. Beyond this fix, the software continues to support a wide array of environments. These include Windows x64 and arm64 using CUDA 12 and 13, as well as various Ubuntu configurations utilizing Vulkan, ROCm 10.0, and OpenVINO. The release also covers Android arm64 and several openEuler options for x86 and aarch64 architectures. While macOS Apple Silicon remains supported, the Intel x64 version for Mac is currently disabled. These adjustments reflect the ongoing effort to keep open-source model tools functional across diverse enterprise and consumer hardware.

German police suspect sabotage after discovering a suspicious object near an electricity substation in Dormagen. This marks the third time this week that devices thought to be targeting the power grid have been found at German substations. These security concerns contrast with the sports world, where Alexander Zverev has advanced to the third round of the US Open. The 2026 French Open winner secured his victory after a marathon five-set match against France's Quentin Halys at Arthur Ashe Stadium in New York City. The clash lasted four hours and 33 minutes, ending after 2 a.m. Zverev admitted he was not happy with his performance but noted that winning ugly is a skill he has mastered. He previously faced another five-set match against Lorenzo Sonego on Wednesday before this latest win.

In Nepal, rescuers have successfully saved two men from a blocked tunnel at the Trishuli 3A Hydropower Station following massive flash floods on the border with Tibet. Tunnelling expert Arnold Dix described the rescue as a series of miracles, noting that the disaster killed 1,300 people and left the landscape unrecognizable. To find the survivors, teams had to use satellite imagery, old topographic maps, and helicopter footage just to locate the tunnel entrance, which had been completely buried by an avalanche. Meanwhile, in the corporate world, organizations are struggling to keep pace with the rapid adoption of artificial intelligence. A virtual event hosted by Dark Reading highlights how the speed of AI integration has left many enterprises scrambling to balance operational power with security. This shift is creating new risks, including a new insider threat model driven by agentic AI and the urgent need for better governance and guardrails.

The war around the Strait of Hormuz has entered a dangerous tanker-for-tanker phase this week. The U.S. is striking Iranian state tankers in retaliation for attacks on commercial shipping, while a laden VLCC sits abandoned and listing off Oman. To counter GPS jamming and spoofing in such conflict zones, the company Q-CTRL recently demonstrated a navigation system using quantum gravimetry to determine a vessel's position without relying on satellites. Meanwhile, in India's Bundelkhand region, recurring droughts are forcing livestock farmers deeper into forests in search of fodder. One farmer, 65-year-old Faujdar Singh Yadav, has been missing for over three months after venturing out with his cattle. In other news, the FDA recently removed a 30-year-old monitoring program for clozapine, a critical drug used to treat serious mental illness and children with psychosis.
After the headlines, back to the weather.
This afternoon will be cloudy with rain chances up to 80 percent and temperatures between 18 and 25 degrees.
And from the weather, a quick look at the calendar.
On your calendar today: Your work calendar has a NAS brainstorm at one in the afternoon. Your personal calendar has Höfische at seven in the evening.
Mail worth checking: You have a payment receipt from PayPal and a notification from Songkick that tickets for Buntspecht are now on sale.
And that's it for your personal morning broadcast.
[mature adult voice, intensely emotional, tender, radiant; hold a long breath after Rise] Rise... and shine.
[very very long pause before speaking; then mature adult voice, most emotional, strong, warm, radiant, deeply encouraging; hold a long breath after Rise] Rise... and shine.
